narration: Here's a quick test — fifty bucks right now, or a hundred next month? Most people take the fifty. That right there is your brain voting to stay broke.
visual: Two glowing option cards side by side — '$50 TODAY' in bright green with glow effect vs '$100 NEXT MONTH' dim and faded — red arrow points to the $50 card with label 'MOST PICK THIS'

narration: It's called hyperbolic discounting — your brain values today's dollar up to seven times more than next year's. It literally can't feel your future self's needs right now.
visual: Brain SVG with convolution folds — giant glowing 'NOW' in red on left, tiny faded 'FUTURE' on right — '7X DEVALUED IN YOUR BRAIN' badge springs in

narration: That's why payday loans charging 391% annual interest still pack their lobbies. People pay fifteen bucks to borrow a hundred — just to get cash today, not Friday.
visual: Payday loan storefront building SVG with sign, windows and door — money flow diagram: $100 borrowed arrow leads to $115 pay-back box — '391% APR' badge in red

narration: You do this every time you skip saving to spend right now. Only 29% of Americans have a three-month emergency fund — your future self keeps losing the vote.
visual: Empty piggy bank SVG beside a calendar with months cycling — progress bar filling to just 29% labeled 'Americans with 3-month emergency fund'

narration: Here's the price tag. Spending an extra $100 a month instead of investing it costs you $122,000 by retirement at seven percent returns. That's what choosing 'now' really costs.
visual: Dual bar chart — left bar 'SPENT' reaches $36K in gray — right bar 'INVESTED AT 7%' grows animated to $122K in green — '$122,000 — THE COST OF NOW' badge in red

narration: Your brain always votes for today, so stop trying to out-think it. Automate savings before the money hits your account and make the future the path of least resistance.
visual: Phone SVG showing auto-transfer app UI — animated money dot flowing from bank to savings automatically — green checkmark — 'AUTOMATE TODAY' CTA button
